content.thinking: Compare the screenshot's events with the game.

content.text:
Yes, these events carry over well. The screenshot shows four, all built on "win levels". Tile-merger has no player levels, so each event needs a merge action to count. The structure, opponents, rankings and rewards can stay as they are.

| Screenshot event | Tile-merger version | What counts |
|---|---|---|
| **Star Rally** | **Tile Rush**: merged tiles drop event marks; collect more than the others in your group | Marks from merges |
| **Shell Hunt** | **Gem Hunt**: special gems on the board give event currency toward a reward track | Gems collected |
| **Boat Race** | **Stack Race**: race four players; each board cleared moves your token one step | Boards cleared |
| **Tide Duel** | **Swap Duel**: clear a board in fewer moves than your rival | Moves per board |

**What needs rethinking for an idle game:**
- **Unlocks:** without player levels, gate the events by location or by lifetime Coins.
- **Fairness:** auto merge, helpers and offline earnings would swamp the rankings. Count only active moves.
- **Opponents:** start with bots and switch to real players later.

I would start with **Stack Race**. It is the simplest to count (boards cleared), automatic play cannot easily game it, and it shows off the board sliding forward.

To take this further: should events be gated by location or by Coins, and do you want bots or real players to start with? Tell me, and I can start a session in tile-merger to write a design doc or build the first event.
I handed the install to the **Project orchestrator · agent-canvas** chat, in auto mode. It will run the type check and tests, build, install, then quit and relaunch Agent canvas.
